ὑδράργυρος.definition: quicksilver, artificially prepared from cinnabar-ore, Dsc.5.95, HeroSpir.1.38, PHolm.4.33, Syn.Alch.p.68 B.; quicksilver and metallic arsenic, Id.p.69 B.; PHolm.2.28

ὑδραύλης.definition: one who plays the POxy.93.2 , Cod.Just.10.48.4; also SIG737.4

ὕδραυλις.definition: hydraulic organ, invented by Ctesibius, Ath.4.174b, cf. Aristocl.ib.c, Ph.Bel.77.43 , HeroSpir.1.28, Simp.in Ph.681.7; described by HeroSpir.1.42:—so Aristocl. l. c., HeroSpir.1.42

ὑδρεῖον.definition: Ion. bucket or pitcher; reservoir, Plb.34.2.6 , Str.12.3.39 : sg. in Id.1.2.30, Supp.Epigr.6.181 , Sardis 7 No. 17.13

ὑδρέλαιον.definition: water mixed with oil, Dsc.2.85, Plu.2.663c, Sor.1.76, Gal.11.534, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.1

ὕδρευμα.definition: watering-place, well, tank, Str.16.4.14, Peripl.M. Rubr.25,26, Ostr.Bodl. iii 245 , Ptol.Geog.1.10.2, Thd.Je.39, 10, OGI701.12 , etc.; irrigation- system, PFlor.50.15 , etc

ὑδρηγός.definition: water-conduit, Hsch. s.v. Suid; water-carrier, Ostr.Bodl. i 316

ὑδρία.definition: water-pot, pitcher, Ar.V.926, Ec.678; vessel of any kind, e. g. wine-pot, Ar.Fr.136; a pot of money, Id.Av.602 ), cf. IG11.161 B100 ; D.47.52; IG22.204.35; bread-pans, POxy.155.4

ὑδριάς.definition: of the water, Pl.Epigr.24, Porph.Antr.13, al., AP6.57

ὑδρίον.definition: Dim. of Hp.Hum.11, acc. to; cistern, reservoir, BGU 117.5

ὑδρίσκη.definition: Dim. of Supp.Epigr.4.187.9 , LXX4 Ki.2.20, Ptol.Euerg.3 J., PLond.2.193.12

ὑδροδρόμος.definition: running in water, i. e. swimming, Orph.H.24.7

ὑδροκέφαλον.definition: water in the head, hydrocephalus, Gal.14.782: as Adj., Antyll. ap. Orib.46.27.1

ὑδροκιρσοκήλη.definition: aneurysm of the vessels of the testicles, Gal.19.448

ὑδρολόγιον.definition: water-clock, Cleom.2.1, Ptol.Tetr.108, PLond.3.1177.245 , Ach.Tat.Intr.Arat.25.6, Procl.Hyp.4.79

ὑδρόμαντις.definition: one who divines from water, Str.16.2.39, Man.4.212

ὑδρομαστευτική.definition: the art of seeking for water, Gp.2.6.1

Ὑδρομέδουσα.definition: Water-queen, name of a frog in Batr.19

ὑδρόμελι.definition: hydromel, later Gr. for Dsc.5.9, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.23.3, S.E.M.6.44, Sor.1.52, Gal.6.274

ὑδρομέτριον.definition: vessel for measuring a flow of water, Ptol.Alm.5.14 , Procl.Hyp.4.71

ὑδρόμηλον.definition: drink of water and Dsc.5.22, Gal.6.744, Artem.1.66, Gp.8.27, etc

ὑδρομύλη.definition: water-mill, Gloss.; also ib., and Hsch

ὑδροπάροχος.definition: one who furnishes water for irrigation, POxy.729.13, 2128.2 , etc.:—hence Supp.Epigr.4.515.10 , POxy.137.22 ; PLond.3.776.19; POxy.1590.10

ὑδροποσία.definition: Ion. water-drinking, Hp.Acut.37, Int.45 , X.Cyr.1.5.12, Pl.Lg.674a, Sor.1.65, etc

ὑδροποτέω.definition: drink water, Hdt.1.71, X.Cyr.6.2.26, Pl.R.561c, Ephor. in PLit.Lond.114, 1 Ep.Ti.5.23, Sor.1.117, is the more correct form acc. to Ammon.Diff.p.111 V

ὑδροπότης.definition: water-drinker, X.Cyr.6.2.29; used of a thin-blooded, mean-spirited fellow, AP11.20 ; cf

ὑδρορόδινον.definition: oil of roses mixed with water, Antyll. ap. Orib.10.13.21, Sor.2.24, etc

ὑδρορρόα.definition: but in Att. also acc. to; a hidden rock in the sea, acc. to Sch.Ar.Ach.1181

ὑδροσεληνίτης.definition: a fine kind of selenite, Dam.Isid.233

ὑδροστάσιμος.definition: of or with standing water, Dsc.3.118

ὑδροστάσιον.definition: standing water, pond; tank, BGU 492.9 , PFay.131.12

ὑδροστατέομαι.definition: Pass., to have stagnant water, spots with standing water, marshes, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v

ὑδροφόρος.definition: Subst. and water-carrier, Hdt.3.14, X.An.4.5.10, PCair.Zen.702.24 , LXXJo.9.33, Luc.Vit.Auct.7, etc.; title of Tragedies by Aeschylus and by Sophocles; title of priestess at Branchidae, OGI226.1 ; so in pl., CIG2885, …

ὑδροφυλακέω.definition: to be a PLond.1.131r.50 ; guard as ib.60; POxy.729.23

ὑδροφύλαξ.definition: guard or inspector of aqueducts or irrigation-works, PLond.1.131r.205 , BGU621.6 , Cod.Just.11.43.10.4, etc

ὑδρόχαρις.definition: Grace of the waters, name of a frog, Batr.227

ὑδροχοεῖον.definition: well, cistern, Men.Prot.p.37 D.; = Lat. aquale, Gloss.:—wrongly written in Suid

ὑδροχόος.definition: water-pourer, name of the; name of an Egyptian month, = POxy.465.11

ὑδροψυγεῖον.definition: cool-water tank, PRyl.233.6 ; written in PLond.2.394.3 , Gloss

ὑδρωπιάω.definition: have dropsy, Hp.Aph.7.47, Aër7, Arist.GA789b14, Thphr.Lass.5, etc

ὑετόμαντις.definition: prophet of rain, Euph.89; Poet. ap. Olymp.in Mete.235.2

ὑηνέω.definition: to be as stupid as a hog, play the hog, Pl.Tht.166c; also Phot

ὑηνία.definition: swinishness, swinish stupidity, Ar.Pax928, Pherecr.237; of the last stage of drunkenness, . . Epich.148; also Phot

ὑΐζω.definition: squeal like a pig, Poll.5.87; v

υἱοθεσία.definition: adoption as a son, Nic.Dam.130.18 J.; in a religious sense, Ep.Rom.8.15, cf. 23, Ep.Gal.4.5; freq. in Inscrr., in the phrase GDI2581.218 , SIG581.102 : pl., D.L.4.53

υἱοποιέομαι.definition: Med., adopt as a son, Plb.36.16.5, GDI2202.24 , D.S.4.60, Nic.Dam.66.7 J.:—Pass., Cat. Cod.Astr.6.71

υἱόω.definition: make into a son, Ael.Fr.180:—Med., adopt as one's son, Nic.Dam.128 J.:—Pass., Suid

υἱωνός.definition: grandson, Il.2.666, Od.24.515, Theoc.17.23, IG5.1450 , POxy.261.7 , SIG829A , Plu.Publ.14, etc.:—fem. J.BJ1.22.1; less Att. than and Moer.p.379 P., p.362 R

ὑλαγμός.definition: barking, baying, Il.21.575, Arist.HA536b30, Aen.Tact.22.14; X.Cyn.4.5

ὑλαγωγέω.definition: carry wood, D.42.7, Poll.7.109:—hence carrying of wood

ὑλάζομαι.definition: fetch or carry wood, IG22.1035.38, 59, 1177.19, Poll.7.109, Hsch

ὑλακή.definition: barking, howling, Poetae ap. Pl.Lg.967d, A.R.3.749, AP6.167 , etc.; also in late Prose, Plu.Cim.18, Luc.VH1.32, prob. l. in Ant.Lib.23.2

ὑλάσκω.definition: = prob. in A.Supp.877 ; pres. Charito6.4, Eust.1791.64; aor. D.C.63.28

ὑλιστήρ.definition: filter, colander, Dsc.2.101, Ath.Med. ap.Orib.5.5.1, PLond.2.191.15

ὑλιστήριον.definition: and = foreg., both in Sch.Nic.Al.493, the latter in POxy.599

ὑλιστήριος.definition: strained, prob. cj. for in Trag.Adesp.420

ὑλόβιος.definition: living in the woods, name of a sect of Indian devotees, being a literal translation of the Skt. Vāna-prastha, one who retired to the forest, being in the third stage of life, Megasth. ap. Str.15.1.60

ὑλονόμος.definition: living in the woods, Simon.179.7; Arist.HA624b29; prob. for in Hp.Vict.2.49; Orph.H.51.10: cf

ὑλοσκόπος.definition: watching over woods, of Pan, Inscr.Cret.1. xvi 7 , AP6.107

ὑλοτομέω.definition: cut or fell wood, Hes.Op.422, D.H.4.44, Dius ap.J.AJ8.5.3

ὑλοτομία.definition: felling of wood, Arist.Pol.1258b31, PLond.3.1171.58 , Ael.NA3.21

ὑλοτόμος.definition: cutting or felling; Subst. woodcutter, woodman, Il.23.123, Hes.Op.807, S.El.98 , IG12.1084.5, Thphr.HP3.9.3, Gal.17.229, etc

ὑλοφορέω.definition: carry or gather wood, Ph.2.86; Phryn.PSp.116B

ὑμέναιος.definition: the wedding or bridal song; = Hymen, the god of marriage, addressed in wedding-songs, freq. in Trag. and Com. , E.Tr.314; ib.331; Ar.Pax1335; Id.Av.1736,1742; Dor. Theoc.18.58; hence the two are used as one word, Opp.…

ὑμενοειδής.definition: membranaceous, Hp.Mul.1.11, Epid.2.2.17, Arist.HA519b13, Dsc.1.106; cf

ὑμενόστρακος.definition: of ware thin as a membrane, Luc.Lex.7

ὑμνογράφος.definition: composer of hymns, of the Psalmist, Ph.1.264, LXX4 Ma.18.15; Ptol. Heph. ap. Phot.Bibl.p.148 B.; ibid

ὑμνοδιδάσκαλος.definition: teacher of hymns, SIG1115.26 , Ath.Mitt.37.302 , Jahresh.15.46 , prob. in IG5.363

ὑμνοθέτης.definition: composer of hymns, lyric poet, Theoc.Ep.11, AP7.428.16 , 12.257 ; a garland of minstrelsy, ib.4.1.2, cf. 44 :—also EM177.25

ὑμνοπολεύω.definition: to be composing songs of praise, PLit.Lond.38.2 :—also Hsch., Phot

ὑμνοπόλος.definition: composing songs of praise; Subst. poet, minstrel, Emp.146, Simon.184, AP7.18 , etc.; Suid., prob. in IG14.1014.1

ὑοσκυαμάω.definition: to be mad from taking henbane: to be raving mad, Pherecr.72:—in Hsch

ὑοσκύαμος.definition: henbane, Hyoscyamus niger, Hp.Morb.2.43, X.Oec.1.13, Dsc.4.68, POxy.1088.39 , Plu.Demetr.20, Sor.2.41, PHolm.21.12, 25.5; other varieties, H. aureus, H. albus, Dsc. l.c.: also PMag.Osl. 1.327

ὑπαγκάλιος.definition: in the arms, of a child, D.H.7.67

ὑπαγκάλισμα.definition: that which is clasped in the arms, a beloved one, of a wife or mistress, S.Tr.540; of a child, E.Tr.757: cf

ὑπαγόρευσις.definition: suggestion, advice, counsel; idea, notion, Gal.1.201

ὑπαγορεύω.definition: the aor. being in Att. (but not in later; suggest, Str.1.2.32,39, cf. Marcellin.Puls.172, Gal.6.314, Posidon. ap. Aët.6.2, etc.; Plu.Marc.29: folld. by inf., D.H.Th.19:—impers. in Pass., Epict.Ench.30

ὑπαγωγίδιον.definition: Dim. of II, Ptol.Harm.2.2, Porph.in Harm.pp.296,307 W

ὑπᾴδω.definition: sing by way of accompaniment, Il.18.570; Od.21.411; Ar.Ra.874; without acc., to accompany with the voice, ib.366; Luc.Salt.30; in poet. form aor. Call.Dian.242; Id.Del.304. [The a of used long by Call.Del. l. c.]

ὑπαίθριος.definition: also E.Andr.227: :—under; as Subst., = Gal.6.94, cf. Hdn.Epim.140

ὑπαικάλλω.definition: = Ael.NA4.45, Fr.107; prob. cj. for in Plu.2.530d

ὑπαινίσσομαι.definition: Att. intimate darkly, hint; allude, glance, D.H.Rh.9.7

ὑπαίρω.definition: aor. Pass. v.l. for in LXX2 Ch.32.23

ὑπαισχύνομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat ashamed, of a thing before a person, Pl.La.179c

ὑπακολουθέω.definition: follow closely, v.l. for in Ph.1.224, etc

ὑπάλειπτρον.definition: spatula for spreading a salve, Hp.Mul.2.163, Art.11, etc.; also Id.Superf.28

ὑπαλείφω.definition: lay on, spread like salve: Med; anoint, Hp.Art.33: metaph., Ar.Ach.1029:—Med., anoint oneself, Hp.Acut.58, Ar.Pax898; paint one's eyes, X.Oec.10.5; Alex.190 ; one anoints himself to fight with the other, Com.Adesp.401…

ὑπάλλαγμα.definition: that which is exchanged; mortgaged property, PRyl.177.13 , etc.; expld. in AB423 as = usage censured by Phryn.275

ὑπάλλαξις.definition: interchange, Gal.1.629, al.; alteration, variation in health, Id.6.403

ὑπαλλάσσω.definition: Att. exchange, Plb.5.8.9; change a little, Plu.2.930c; Gal.10.160; Id.6.28, cf. 307, al.; alter the text of a book, Id.15.21, cf. 16.679, al.:—Med., change one's place, Poll.6.194; change one's bearing, Phot., Suid. s…

ὑπαμφιέννυμαι.definition: Med., put on under another garment, Ael.NA16.15

ὑπαναγιγνώσκω.definition: read clause by clause, Is.11.4, Aeschin.2.109; Hyp.Eux.40; read aloud, Hierocl.in CA27p.484M

ὑπαναδύομαι.definition: Med., withdraw secretly from, endeavour to escape, D.H.7.13: abs., Com.Adesp.19.3 D

ὑπανακαθαίρω.definition: purge gently, cj. for in Sor.1.86

ὑπανάκειμαι.definition: Pass., recline below at table, D.L.7.17

ὑπανακινέω.definition: intr., rise up and go away, Ar.Ec.1165

ὑπανακλάω.definition: bend up under, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.75

ὑπαναλίσκω.definition: waste away, spend or consume gradually; spend as a contribution, . . BMus.Inscr. 425

ὑπαναμιμνήσκομαι.definition: recall to mind once more, Aesop.157H

ὑπαναπείθω.definition: exert undue influence upon, Mitteis Chr.96 ii 11, cf. 18

ὑπαναπίμπλαμαι.definition: Pass., to be filled gradually, with . . , Ael.NA17.13

ὑπανάστασις.definition: rising up from one's seat, Arist.EN1165a28, cf. Phld.Hom.p.36O.: pl., Pl.R.425b, Porph.Abst.2.61: cf. 2

ὑπαναφλέγομαι.definition: Pass., to be heated gradually, Ael.VH14.41

ὑπαναφύομαι.definition: grow or swell up under or gradually, ib.7, NA4.21

ὑπαναχωρέω.definition: go back gradually, retire slowly, Th.1.51; D.H.5.8, cf. S.E.M.9.293, D.C.63.26; of death, PMasp.151.37

ὑπανερπύζω.definition: creep up secretly or softly, Ael.NA5.3

ὑπανθέω.definition: begin to flower or blossom, Philostr.Im.1.31, Poll.1.60; Id.2.10

ὑπανιάομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat distressed, opt. Ar.Nu.1195

ὑπανίσταμαι.definition: Pass. with aor. 2 and pf. Act., rise; rise up from their seats to make room or show respect to . . , Hdt.2.80, cf. Phld.Vit.p.38J.; Ar.Nu.993 ; X.Lac.15.6; Id.Hier.7.2, cf. Smp.4.31; Id.Mem.2.3.16: metaph., gave way, …

ὑπάντησις.definition: Astrol., encounter of a heavenly body, in Ptol.Tetr.132; metaph., retort, answer, S.E.M.11.202; ib.7.278, A.D.Synt.305.19

ὑπαντήτωρ.definition: heavenly body encountered in course of projection of vital quadrant, Heph.Astr.2.11.72.28), Doroth.inCat.Cod. Astr.2.198.15, Sch.Ptol.Tetr.169

ὑπάντομαι.definition: only in pres. and impf., = Hdn.4.11.2, 8.7.8

ὑπάπειμι.definition: withdraw, retreat, Th.5.9; withdraw stealthily, Id.3.111; Luc.Icar.14; . . was past the age of . . , Philostr.VA6.3

ὑπαπολείπομαι.definition: Pass., to be left behind , ib.10.43

ὑπαράσσω.definition: Att. strike underneath, Anon. ap. Suid

ὑπάργυρος.definition: having silver underneath: hence; of rocks and the like , containing silver, veined with silver, E.Cyc.294, Rh.970; X.Vect.1.5, 4.2: metaph. of men, containing a proportion of silver, Pl.R.415c; cf

ὑπαρχιτέκτων.definition: deputy clerk of the works, IG22.1678aA7 , Delph.3.25 ii A 13 , PPetr.2p.138, al. , IG7.3073.160

ὑπαρχιφυλακίτης.definition: deputy chief of police, BGU1222.61, al

ὕπαρχος.definition: subordinate commander, lieutenant; subordinate governor, of satraps, etc., Hdt.3.70, 4.166, al., X.An.4.4.4; Th.8.31; Sor.Vit.Hippocr.8; in the Seleucid kingdom, OGI225.36

ὑπαρωματίζω.definition: have something of an aromatic flavour, Dsc.3.8

ὑπασθενέω.definition: to be a little unwell, Phryn.PSp.120B

ὑπασπίδιος.definition: covered with a shield, in Hom. only as Adv., and Il.13.158, 807, 16.609:—after Hom.as Adj., AsiusFr.Ep.13.7 K.; the body-armour and arms of Ajax, S.Aj.1408 ; sleep an armed sleep, sleep in arms, E.Rh.740

ὑπαστράπτω.definition: flash or gleam by reflection, Philostr.VA2.24

ὑπασχολέομαι.definition: to be a subordinate official, OGI179.10

ὑπαυλέω.definition: play on the flute in accompaniment, Alcm.78; D.C.74.5; Posidon.4J.; Luc.Harm.1: abs., Id.Salt.83

ὑπαφίσταμαι.definition: step back, withdraw, Antipho4.4.1; Men.Sam.153; Thales ap.D.L.1.44; Ael.NA2.25

ὑπαχλύνομαι.definition: Pass., grow dark by degrees, Q.S.1.67

ὑπεγείρω.definition: rouse gradually, Philostr.VS1.21.5; Id.Im.1.24, cf. Ael.NA6.1

ὑπέγκειμαι.definition: form an inner layer, cj. for in Sor.1.57

ὑπειλέομαι.definition: Pass., wriggle, creep under, Ael.NA9.57; glossed by Hp. ap. Gal.19.148; of a bandage, to be passed under, Heliod. ap. Orib.48.51.1

ὑπεισβαίνω.definition: steal into, cj. Housman in E.Med.382

ὑπεισδύομαι.definition: Med. with aor. 2 Act. get in secretly, slip or steal in, Hdt.1.12 ; come or go in gradually, Arist.GC325b4:—Act. pres. EM290.13

ὑπεισέρχομαι.definition: enter upon secretly; come into one's mind, Luc.Merc.Cond.11

ὑπεκβαίνω.definition: go out from below, Anon. ap. Suid. s.v. of a vein, Gal.2.793; escaping . . , Agath.4.28, cf. 5.1,20

ὑπεκβάλλω.definition: cast out, reject, AP5.65; f.l. for in Plu.2.530d

ὑπεκδιδράσκω.definition: only in aor. run out, escape secretly from, Plu.2.642b; Id.Flam.20: abs., D.C.36.24

ὑπεκδύομαι.definition: Med., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., slip out of, escape, c. acc., E.Cyc.347, cf. Plu.2.170f, Opp.H.3.384, etc.: metaph., Phld.Sto.Herc.339.13: also c. gen., Plu.Dem.9: abs., having slipped out, Hdt.1.10, Plu.Arat.9, etc.;…

ὑπεκθέσιμος.definition: of merchandise, deposited for re- exportation, GDI5040.25 ; cf. II

ὑπεκκαθαίρω.definition: purge from beneath, in Pass., Hp.Mul.1.60, Nat.Mul.35

ὑπεκκαίω.definition: kindle, Thphr.Ign.63: metaph., stir up, Luc.Peregr.26; inflame, Plu.2.616e; Id.Dio22

ὑπεκκαλύπτω.definition: uncover from below or a little, AP7.480

ὑπεκκαύστρια.definition: she who lights a fire underneath, name of the priestess of Athene at Soli, Plu.2.292a Hsch.)

ὑπέκκειμαι.definition: Pass., to be carried out to a place of safety, to be stowed safe away, Hdt.8.41,9.73, Th.8.31; of money, Th.1.137; Isoc.19.18.— cf. I

ὑπεκκλέπτω.definition: carry off secretly, J.AJ14.11.6, Opp.H.4.48:—Pass., Plu.Them.25

ὑπεκκομίζω.definition: carry out or away to safety, Th.4.123, Plu.Cam.21; eliminate insensibly, Ruf. ap. Orib.45.30.51:—Med., get all one's goods carried out to safety, Hdt.9.6, cf. X.Cyr.2.4.13

ὑπεκκρίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be carried off insensibly, D.L.9.76

ὑπεκλείπω.definition: fail or flag by degrees, Thphr.Ign.55, Gal.8.489

ὑπεκλύω.definition: loosen or weaken a little, Plu.Nic.14; J.BJ7.8.5; Sor.2.61 ; Ps.-Dsc.1.103; Sch.Il.6.260; weaken the force of, A.D.Synt.224.4:—Pass., cease, become weaker and weaker, Hp.Mul.1.25; Sch.Ar.V.151; S.E.M.11.214, cf. Sor.2…

ὑπεκπέμπω.definition: send out secretly, Th.4.8; E.Hec.6; Id.Andr.47:—Pass., c. acc. loci, to Phocis, S.El.1350

ὑπεκπεράω.definition: go forth and pass over, Q.S.5.246, cf. Orph.A.69

ὑπεκπίπτω.definition: miss, J.AJ16.11.5; prolapse, cj. in Sor.1.12

ὑπεκπονέω.definition: work out under another's command, Poll.9.110

ὑπεκπροθρῴσκω.definition: aor. part. spring out from under, Opp.C.4.160

ὑπεκπροχέομαι.definition: Pass., stream forth from under, Q.S.13.57

ὑπεκρέω.definition: flow out from under, Philostr.Im.1.12; metaph., pass away gradually, Pl.Smp.203e; opp. Arist.GC321b27, Plot.4.4.42; c. acc., Plu.Mar.46; of a person, having slipped out of the tent, Id.Pomp.3

ὑπεκρήγνυμαι.definition: Pass., to be gradually broken away, Plu.Cam.3

ὑπεκτρέπω.definition: turn gradually or secretly from a thing, S.Tr.549:—Med., turn aside from, c. acc., Pl.Phd.108b: c. inf., decline the task of helping . . , S.OC566

ὑπεκτρέχω.definition: fut. Id.Ant.1086: aor; run out beyond, S.Tr.167

ὑπεμφαίνω.definition: hint at, indicate, S.E.M.1.4, Gal.19.556; intr., to be cogent, of a proof, Papp.650.5

ὑπεξέχω.definition: intr., withdraw or retire secretly, Hdt.5.72; Id.8.132; Id.6.74

ὑπεραγαπάω.definition: love exceedingly, make much of, c. acc., D.23.196, Arist.EN1168a1; for a thing, J.AJ12.4.6

ὑπεραγωνίζομαι.definition: Med., fight for, J.BJ2.12.7, App.BC1.96, Jul.Or.2.55c; Them.Or.2.37a

ὑπεραιδέομαι.definition: feel great shame before, stand in great awe of, c. acc., A.R.3.978

ὑπεραισχύνομαι.definition: Pass., feel much ashamed, . . Aeschin.3.151; Id.1.33: c. part., to be ashamed at doing a thing, Dromo1

ὑπεραιωρέω.definition: suspend or support above; hold up, raise, Aret.CD1.3:—Pass., of the overlapping end of a dislocated bone, to be lifted or drawn over, Hp.Art.70; ib.71, Fract.14, cf. 41: abs., Id.Art.22: Littré gives the Act. in same …

ὑπερακμάζω.definition: surpass in vigour or bloom, Myro2 J.: abs., PSI6.666.18

ὑπερακοντίζω.definition: overshoot, i. e. outdo, Ar.Av.363 ; I overshot him with my 200 kine, Id.Eq.659, cf. Diph.66.5; also has outdone them in stealing, Ar.Pl.666:—Pass., has been made to excel . . , Alex.Aphr.Pr.2Prooem

ὑπερακούω.definition: pf. hear exceedingly well, Phryn.PSp.121 B

ὑπεράλγεινος.definition: in excessive anguish, f. l. in Aristid.Or.48.63

ὑπεραναβαίνω.definition: pass over, cross, Zos.2.53; rise above, Gal.19.172

ὑπεραναιδεύομαι.definition: Pass., to be surpassed in impudence, Ar.Eq.1206 ; Dind. suggests citing AB80

ὑπερανάκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie above another at table, D.L.7.17 codd

ὑπεραναλίσκω.definition: also overspend, exceed estimate, PCair. Zen.702.17, al. , PHib.1.100.1 , Sammelb.7451.65 :—Pass., PCair.Zen.176.2 ; Supp.Epigr.4.447.60

ὑπερανίεμαι.definition: to be excessively diluted, Crito ap.Gal.13.880

ὑπερανίσταμαι.definition: Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act., stand up or project over, c. gen., D.H.1.15, 9.68: abs., Id.3.68, Luc.Icar.12: metaph., strutting, conceited, Philostr.Her.15

ὑπεραντλέομαι.definition: Pass., to be very leaky, to be water-logged, Luc.Merc.Cond.2

ὑπέραντλος.definition: prop. of a ship, full of water; of persons, Diph.43.12: metaph., over-charged, Luc.Tim.18; E.Hipp.767 ; Plu.Mar.45

ὑπεραπατάομαι.definition: Pass., to be deceived excessively, AP9.761

ὑπεραπλόομαι.definition: Pass., to be super-simplified or transcendent in simplicity, Iamb.Myst.7.2, Procl.Inst.93: c. gen., Id.in R.1.73K., al., Eustr.in EN268.31

ὑπεραποδίδωμι.definition: pay over and above, IPE12.32A18 , Philostr.VS1.25.3

ὑπεραποκρίνομαι.definition: Med., answer for one, defend him, Ar.V.951, Th.186

ὑπεραπόλλυμι.definition: destroy and more than destroy, v.l. for; Pass., die for, Sch.Pi.P.6.30

ὑπεραπολογέομαι.definition: speak for any one, defend him, Hdt.6.136, X.HG1.7.16; Antipho2.4.2

ὑπεραποχράω.definition: to be more than enough, Poll.1.236, 6.149. Adv. pres.part.Act. more than enough, Id.9.154

ὑπεραρπάζομαι.definition: to be 'rapt' above, Procl.in Prm.p.839 S

ὑπεραρρωδέω.definition: Ion. for to be afraid on behalf of, for Hellas, Hdt.8.72

ὑπερασπάζομαι.definition: to be exceedingly fond of, X.Smp.4.38, Plu.2.229e

ὑπερασπίζω.definition: fut. LXXPr.2.7, al.: pf. OGI441.80 :—cover with a shield, Plb.6.39.6, D.S.17.99, D.H.6.12, Plu.Cor.3, Arr.Fr.56 J., etc.; Id.An.6.28.4, LXXGe.15.1, al.; ib.4 Ki.19.34: metaph. c. gen., defend, Chor.32.1

ὑπερασπισμός.definition: a covering with a shield, protection, LXXPs.17.36, al

ὑπερασπιστής.definition: one who holds a shield over, protector, champion, ib.2,30, al., cf. Ph.1.374: fem. LXX4 Ma.15.29

ὑπεραστράπτω.definition: flash exceedingly, Arr.Cyn.4.5; c. acc., outshine, Procop.Aed.1.4

ὑπεραυγέω.definition: = foreg., in Pass., prob. l. in Str.16.4.6

ὑπεραυχέω.definition: to be over-proud, Th.4.19, D.C.57.12, etc

ὑπεράχθομαι.definition: Pass., to be exceedingly grieved at . . , c. dat., Hdt.6.21; S.El.177

ὑπερβαρής.definition: exceedingly heavy, A.Ag.1175 ; . . IGRom.4.1302 ; POxy.486.32 :—but in Hp.Art.46, Gal.7.587

ὑπερβατήριος.definition: of or for passing over, Polyaen.1.10.1; cf

ὑπερβιάζομαι.definition: press exceeding heavily, of the plague, Th.2.52, cf. J.AJ9.10.2, Procop.Vand.2.4, al

ὑπερβλύζω.definition: bubble or gush over, overflow, Hp.Ep.23, cf. Q.S.5.324; Ph.1.174; D.Chr.12.70; Philostr.VA3.14; ib.25: metaph. of wine- drinkers, Ph.2.478 : c. acc., Q.S.11.192; Procop.Aed.1.7: c. dat., Herm.in Phdr.p.170A

ὑπερβόλιον.definition: overbid, PTeb.72.418, 61.408,416; increase of rent, PTeb.302.14 , POxy.103.26

ὑπερβράζω.definition: boil or foam over, in aor. Pass., AP11.248

ὑπεργάνυμαι.definition: exult much, Philostr.Im.1.5; rejoice over, Eun.VSp.468 B

ὑπεργέμω.definition: to be overfull, of a thing, Alex.83, Plb.4.75.8; Trag.Adesp.486: abs., Alex.216, D.S.3.17

ὑπεργεννάομαι.definition: Pass., to be born besides, Hsch. s.v

ὑπεργηράω.definition: grow exceedingly old, Poll.9.18, Men.Mon.608: pf. Apollod. ap. D.L.8.52, Aët.16.26

ὑπεργίγνομαι.definition: have the superiority, Phld.Rh.2.86S; of Time, elapse, BGU1167.7 , cf. 1148.14

ὑπερδάκνω.definition: in Pass., to be excessively irritated , Archig. ap. Gal.13.255

ὑπερδείδω.definition: fear for one, S.Ant.82; fear exceedingly, Them.Or.10.138c: abs., to be in exceeding fear, Hdt.8.94

ὑπερδειμαίνω.definition: to be much afraid of, Hdt.5.19

ὑπερδεκατάλαντος.definition: of more than ten talents, Phalar.Ep.137.1

ὑπερδιαζεύγνυμαι.definition: to be separated by an interval of an octave, Bacch.Harm.87: hence ibid

ὑπερδιαθήκη.definition: codicil, L. Robert Villes d' Asie Mineure 226

ὑπερδιατείνω.definition: overstretch or -strain; Pass., strain or exert oneself above measure, D.25.1 , D.Chr.50.6, Luc.Herm.26, etc

ὑπερδιαφορέομαι.definition: Pass., to be dissipated in excess, Sor.2.54

ὑπέρδικος.definition: more than just, severely just; pleading for another, Sch.Pl.Phd.86e

ὑπερδισκεύω.definition: throw the discus farther than another, c. acc., Phryn.PSp.117 B

ὑπερδιψάω.definition: to be exceedingly thirsty, Gal.12.288, 351, UP11.10

ὑπερδομέομαι.definition: Pass., to be built over, J.BJ6.3.2

ὑπερείδω.definition: fut. Diog.Oen.20: pf. Pass; lean upon, LXXJb.8.15

ὑπέρεικος.definition: St. John's wort, Hypericum crispum, Nic.Al.603:—more freq. Dsc.3.154, Gal.12.148; also, Hypericum revolutum, Dsc.1.19

ὑπερεισοδιάζω.definition: contribute on behalf of , IGRom.3.739 iii 89

ὑπερεκβλύζω.definition: bubble or boil over, superabound, Al.Pr.3.10

ὑπερεκθεραπεύω.definition: seek to win by excessive attention, Aeschin.2.154

ὑπερεκλάμπω.definition: to be very bright, of the eyes, Id.16.782

ὑπερεκπίπτω.definition: extend beyond, exceed, c. gen; abs., go beyond all bounds, Luc.Herm.67; . . Id.Salt.83, cf. S.E.M.6.6

ὑπερεκτρέπομαι.definition: Pass., feel utter aversion for, Aret.SD1.5

ὑπερεκφεύγω.definition: survive a certain period, c. acc., Hp.Morb.2.58; escape from, Plot.6.6.3

ὑπερέκχυσις.definition: overflowing, of the Nile, Hld.1.5; of the sea, Plu.2.731c ; Gloss

ὑπερεμφορέομαι.definition: Pass., to be filled quite full, Luc.DMeretr.6.3: abs., Id.Ep.Sat.32

ὑπερενόομαι.definition: Pass., to be completely one, Iamb.Myst.2.11

ὑπερεντελής.definition: more than complete, f.l. in D.C.47.17

ὑπερεντρυφάω.definition: to be exceedingly haughty, to us, Alciphr.1.37; in or by . . , Sch.S.Tr.281

ὑπερεξαίρω.definition: raise exceedingly: Pass., Hp.Epid.4.31; exalt or praise exceedingly, Eust.1265.25

ὑπερεπαινέω.definition: praise above measure, or Hdt.1.8, Ar.Eq.680, Ec.186, Pl.Euthd.303b, al

ὑπερεπαίρω.definition: exalt or exaggerate beyond measure, App.Pun.42, Syr.12, BC1.11

ὑπερεπιθυμέω.definition: desire exceedingly, c. inf., X.Cyr.4.3.21, 6.1.5, Sm. Ps.118.174, Porph.Plot.19

ὑπερεπιτείνω.definition: strain too tight, to be too rigid; trans., increase the force of, Artem.3.59

ὑπερέρχομαι.definition: aor. 2 pf. over; surpass, excel, Pi.O.13.15

ὑπερευδαιμονέω.definition: to be exceedingly happy, Arist.Rh.1385b21, Luc.Gall.20 , Aristaenet.1.18

ὑπερευδαίμων.definition: gen. utterly blessed, Plot.5.8.4,5; cf. foreg

ὑπερευρίσκω.definition: fetch or cost a higher amount, IG7.3074.2 ; because the expenses came to more, dub. in PLips.97 xxvii 21, xxxii 16

ὑπερευφραίνω.definition: delight exceedingly, Phld.Po.2.17, Lib.Ep.243:—Pass., rejoice exceedingly, Luc.Am.5; at . . , Id.Icar.2; J.BJ7.1.3

ὑπερηγορέω.definition: speak for, Dam. ap. Suid., cf. Ascl.in Metaph.201.11

ὑπερηνόρεος.definition: Dor. = sq., Theoc.29.19, but f.l. for

ὑπερθαυμάζω.definition: c. acc., wonder greatly at, admire greatly, J.BJ2.9.3, Luc.Zeux.3, Gal.18.401, Ath.12.523d

ὑπερθεματίζω.definition: overbid, Gloss., Dosith.p.431 K., Priscian. de xii vers.Aen.116

ὑπερθεραπεύω.definition: cherish or court exceedingly, Poll.4.49, Hld.1.9

ὑπερθερμαίνω.definition: warm or heat excessively, Hp.Morb.1.2:—Pass., ib.2.1, Arist.Pr.860b19, EE1239b35, Thphr.HP4.14.6, Alex.Aphr.Pr.1.89, Placit.5.30.6

ὑπέρθεσις.definition: putting over or across; = I. I. pass, Str.16.2.8, al

ὑπερθνήσκω.definition: die for, E.Alc.682; Id.Ph.998, cf. Andr.498 : abs., Id.Alc.155

ὑπερθρασύνομαι.definition: Pass., act with great audacity, D.C.41.28

ὑπερθυμόομαι.definition: Med., to be inf. Poll.5.125; impf. D.C.43.37

ὑπεριδρύω.definition: in Pass., to be established above, superior to, HeroDef.136.23, Procl.Inst.98, Dam.Pr.26

ὑπεριζάνω.definition: sit on, Nonn.D.41.308; settle upon, J.AJ3.5.2

ὑπερινάω.definition: purge violently, Hp. as cited by Erot. , Poll.4.179

ὑπέρινος.definition: purged violently, Id.Epid.6.5.15, Demetr.Com.Vet.6, Ruf. ap. Orib.7.26.168; Thphr.HP9.14.2; exhausted by production, Arist.GA750a29

ὑπερίπταμαι.definition: later form for Arist.Mir.836a33, Plu.Num.8; Max.Tyr.6.6

ὑπερισθμίζω.definition: draw or convey over an isthmus, Plb.4.19.9, 5.101.4, al

ὑπερίσταμαι.definition: Pass., with aor. 2 and pf. Act.:—stand; stand over one for protection, protect, S.El.188 : abs., A.R.4.370

ὑπερισχύω.definition: to be exceedingly strong, of fire; of persons, to be overbearing, Sammelb. 4638.6

ὑπερκαθαίρομαι.definition: Pass., to be purged excessively, Hp.Aph.7.41, cf. Gal.18.144

ὑπερκαθίστημι.definition: Dor. inf. pay on another's behalf, Leg.Gort.11.35

ὑπερκαίω.definition: burn violently, be exceedingly hot, of the sun, Philostr.Gym.58; Poll.5.110:—Pass., to be burnt up, Alex.Aphr.Pr.2.74: metaph., Sch.Il.9.421

ὑπερκάμνω.definition: suffer or labour for any one; in pf., gloss on Sch.S.Tr.791

ὑπερκαταβακχεύω.definition: talk arrogantly, prob. cj. in Com.Adesp.1380

ὑπερκατάκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie or sit above, at table, c. gen., Id.Mar.3, Luc.Symp.31, etc

ὑπερκατεργάζομαι.definition: aor. 1 part. in pass. sense, over-digested, Gal.6.255

ὑπερκαχλάζω.definition: run bubbling or boiling over, Luc.DMar.11.2; Philostr.Jun.Im.11

ὑπέρκειμαι.definition: Pass., lie above, esp. of place, to be; metaph., to be placed above , superior, Plot.3.4.3, cf. Procl.Inst.56; transcend, Dam.Pr.164: c. acc., excel, LXXEz.16.47

ὑπερκενόω.definition: purge completely or excessively, Gal.17.365:— Pass., Id.7.602, Phryn.PSp.120 B

ὑπερκέρασις.definition: an outflanking on one wing, Plb.1.27.5, Ascl.Tact.10.2, Arr.Tact.29.9, Ael.Tact.25.1, 38.1; cf. sq. and

ὑπερκορέννυμι.definition: over-fill or glut, one with a thing, Thgn.1158, in aor. opt. pf. inf. Poll.7.23

ὑπερκορής.definition: over-full, glutted, D.C.51.24, cf. 59.17, 60.34, Poll.5.151: metaph., sens. obsc., Ptol.Euerg.3 J. Adv. Poll.5.151

ὑπερκρατέω.definition: overpower, LXX3 Ki.16.22; intr., prevail, ib.6.10.2

ὑπερκρεμάννυμι.definition: hang up over, Pi.O.1.57 ; PMag.Berol.2.49:—Pass., Thgn.1022, cf. Mimn.5

ὑποδημάτιον.definition: Dim. of Hp.Art.62; of the shoes of an ass, Arr.Epict.4.1.80

ὑποδηματουργός.definition: sandalmaker, JHS22.124 , prob. in Wiener Denkschr.44.27 No.59

ὑποδῃόομαι.definition: Pass., to be treated in hostile manner, Q.S.2.260, 3.355

ὑποδιαβιβρώσκομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat corroded, Hp.Cord.6

ὑποδιαίρεσις.definition: subdivision, Diog.Bab.Stoic.3.215, Gal.14.689, Hermog.Inv.3.10, S.E.M.11.15, Vett.Val.98.10, Procl.Hyp.3.10, etc

ὑποδιακονέω.definition: serve under another, CIG1947.8 :—Med., Poll.4.92, cf. Arg.Theoc.2

ὑποδιαλείπω.definition: intermit a little, of the pulse, Gal.8.487

ὑποδιανοέομαι.definition: Med., design secretly, v.l. in Jul.Ep.107

ὑποδιαπήγνυμαι.definition: Pass., with pf. 2 to be fixed across below, Ph.Bel.74.11

ὑποδιαστολή.definition: slight stop, between words in speaking; mark to divide words from one another , e. g. to distinguish it from Ps.-D.T.674, Sch.D.T.p.24H., al., Eust.701.56, 1465.16

ὑποδίδωμι.definition: intr., give way, Arist.MA698b15; Aristid.Or.31.12, Philostr.VA3.20; of power and empire, decay, Aristid.2.187 J., Philostr.VS1.21.4; in strength, Id.Gym.48

ὑποδιπλάσιος.definition: the inverse of double, i. e. 1/2, Nicom.Ar.1.18

ὑποδομή.definition: Dor. supporting wall, = II, IG4.823.36 , 11.146 A72 , 158 A72 , al

ὑποδοχεῖον.definition: reservoir, Aristeas89,91, PTeb.733.8 ; used for storage of fish, PHamb.6.10 ; of wine, PSI8.918.2 , POxy.729.28 ; PPetr.2p.64 ; coupled with PSI9.1056.6 ; perh. also, store-house, barn, BGU301.11 , cf. PTeb.86.15, al.…

ὑποδοχεύς.definition: receiver, host, Luc.Fug.30, Charito3.2, Phot. s.v. Astrol., of a planet entertaining another, Vett.Val.103.1

ὑποδοχή.definition: entertainment, hospitality, Ar.Pax530 , Pl.Lg.919a ; . . Hdt.7.119; . . E.IA1229; Ath.5.210e; SIG1107.12 ; also for the reception of the army , Th.7.74

ὑποδράσσομαι.definition: Att. Med., try to get hold of, Plu.Caes.14 codd

ὑποδράω.definition: Ep. serve, c. dat., Od.15.333; Ael.NA9.33

ὑπόδρομος.definition: name for a venomous spider, = Ael.NA6.26; = IV, a place for ships to run into, cove, Ph.1.14, al., Ptol.Geog.4.6.2

ὑποδυσφορέω.definition: to be somewhat restless or impatient, Pl.Ep.357e

ὑποδυσωπέομαι.definition: Pass., look somewhat askance at, Plu.2.646b

ὑποδύτης.definition: garment worn under a coat of mail, PEnteux.32.6 , D.S.17.44, Plu.Phil.11; simply undergarment, LXXEx.28.31, IG5.1390.20 , J.BJ5.5.7

ὑποδώριος.definition: hypo-Dorian, Ath.14.625a; Plu.2.1142f:—Adv. in the hypo-Dorian mode, Arist.Pr.920a8, 922b10

ὑποεπιμερής.definition: = Ph.2.183 cod. M, cf. Iamb.in Nic.p.37 P

ὑποζύγιον.definition: beast for the yoke, beast of; later specifically an ass, LXXZa.9.9, Ev.Matt.21.5, 2 Ep.Pet.2.16; PCair.Zen.158, ; PPetr.3p.56 ; Hp.Aph.4.70

ὑποζυμόομαι.definition: Pass., ferment slightly, Dieuch. ap. Orib.4.5.1

ὑποζώννυμι.definition: brace a ship, so as to make her seaworthy , IG l. c., Plb. l. c., Act.Ap.27.17; IG22.1621.68

ὑποθειάζω.definition: to be divinely inspired, Philostr.VA1.3, cf. 6.11

ὑποθεραπεύω.definition: to be disposed to worship, Philostr.VA4.40; bribe, Memn.24

ὑπόθερμος.definition: somewhat hot, Gal.6.240, Poll.5.108: of persons, somewhat hot or passionate, Hdt.6.38, cf. Luc.Cal.5; of a horse, Poll.1.192; Plu.2.1146f

ὑποθέτης.definition: one who suggests, prompter, adviser, Anon. ap. Suid

ὑποθεωρέω.definition: hold up and look at, Plu.2.42c

ὑποθηκάριος.definition: of or for a mortgage, Just.Nov.4.2, Procop.Arc.28: in Lat. form hypothecarius, Cod.Just.4.32.26, al

ὑποθήκη.definition: suggestion, counsel, warning; pledge, deposit, mortgage, D.34.50, Arist.Oec.1348b21, Supp.Epigr.1.366.39 , PCair.Zen.504.4 , PEnteux.15.4 , etc.; PRein.18.11 ; upon securities given, SIG742.39, cf. 51 , al.; mortgages…

ὑποθηκιμαῖος.definition: relating to a mortgage, PMasp.23.11 , 96.15 ; = fiduciarius, Gloss.: neut. pledge, PMasp.96.38

ὑποθλίβω.definition: press under or gently, Nic.Th.296 codd. , Al.30, Dsc.1.43, Luc.VH2.14, Cass.Pr.28

ὑποθορυβέω.definition: begin to make a clamour, Th.4.28

ὑποθρύπτομαι.definition: Pass., to be nerveless or emasculated; I wantoned with her face—by stealing kisses, AP5.293.15

ὑποθυμίασις.definition: Ion. fumigation, Hp.Nat.Mul.103 , Dsc.1.67, Sor.2.33, Hippiatr.22

ὑποθωπεύω.definition: win by flattery, Ar.Ach.639 , V.610 , D.H.7.34, Philostr.VS1.21.4: abs., without using any flattery, Hdt.1.30; Chor.3.84p.69 F.-R

ὑποίγνυμι.definition: open a little or secretly, Ar.Th.424, cf. Ec.15

ὑποικίζομαι.definition: in aor. 1 Med., = foreg. I, AP7.372

ὑποικοδομέω.definition: build under, IG 22.463.114; f. l. for Luc.Hist.Conscr.3

ὑποικουρέω.definition: keep house, stay at home, Ael.NA11.32; trans., engage in or plot underhand, . . Ar.Th.1168, cf. Plu.Pomp.42:—Pass., anger secretly cherished, Plb.4.49.4, cf. 3.11.3: the plot, intrigue, Ph.2.202

ὑποΐσχομαι.definition: Med., catch by holding under, A.R.4.473; ib.169

ὑποκαθαίρω.definition: purge downwards, Hp.Aph.7.68, cf. Thphr.HP7.12.3, Plu.2.127c, Gal.6.248

ὑποκαθέζομαι.definition: lie in ambush, Anon. ap. Suid., Onos.6.7; late aor. sink, settle down, Sch.Th.3.89, Gp.6.18

ὑποκαθίζω.definition: place in ambush; intr. in Act., lie in ambush, Plb.12.4.14, etc

ὑποκαθίσταμαι.definition: Pass., settle at the bottom, of; subside, of symptoms, Aret.CA1.1

ὑποκαπνίζω.definition: burn for purpose of fumigation, Hp.Mul.2.117, cf. Gal.14.551

ὑποκαπνισμός.definition: fumigation, Dsc.Eup.1.210, Antyll. ap. Orib.8.12.1, Sor.2.33, Gal.16.147

ὑποκαταβαίνω.definition: descend by degrees, Hdt.2.15; go back gradually, i. e. relax severity of régime, Hp.Aph.1.7

ὑποκατάβασις.definition: gradual descent, Eust.1402.16; glossed by Phot., Suid.; reduction, Gal.17.378

ὑποκαταγελάω.definition: laugh in one's sleeve at, Arr.Epict.4.6.21

ὑποκατακλίνω.definition: lay down under:—Pass., lie down; Pass. also, lie or sit lower at table, ib.618e; J.AJ12.4.9

ὑποκατάκλισις.definition: metaph., taking a lower place, compliance, servility, Plu.2.58c ; a humiliation, Hld.10.25

ὑποκαταπίπτω.definition: sink down under, Ep. aor. Q.S.1.588

ὑποκατασκευάζω.definition: prepare secretly, J.AJ15.4.2; ib.16.1.2 ; prepare beforehand, Iamb.Myst.3.27 ; should be somewhat more studied, Demetr.Eloc.224

ὑπόκαυσις.definition: burning underneath, Dieuch. ap; burning of bricks, POxy.2153.12

ὑπόκαυστος.definition: heated by a hypocaust, Herod.Med. in Rh.Mus.58.112

ὑπόκειμαι.definition: used as Pass. of fut; of places, lie close to, Isoc.4.108; Aeschin.3.118; Plu.Crass.29; Arist.Mete.364a7, cf.Pr.941b39; Gp.2.5.1; the adjacent soil, D.S.3.50; the adjacent country, ibid. ; Plb.5.59.4 codd. ; Id.3.74.2…

ὑποκελεύω.definition: do the duty of a boatswain, give the time in rowing, Luc.Cat.19:—hence Sch. ad loc

ὑπόκενος.definition: somewhat hollow, Ruf.Onom.139, v.l. in Dsc.2.131; simply, hollow, PMag.Par.1.2361; somewhat flabby, Mnesith. ap. Orib.inc.15.8: metaph., Hsch. s.v. ; Hermog.Id.2.9; Hierocl.in CA23p.470 M

ὑποκινδυνεύω.definition: run some risk, f. l. for in Plu.Pel.2

ὑποκινέω.definition: move softly or lightly; metaph., urge gently on, so as to make him speak, Pl.Chrm.162d, Plu.Aem.9; Luc.Eun.13; cf. A.II.2

ὑποκιρσόω.definition: in Pass., of veins, to be swollen, Hp.Ulc.10

ὑποκλυσμός.definition: purging from below, as by a clyster, Plu.2.974c

ὑπόκοιλος.definition: slightly concave, Hp.VC13, Dsc.3.90, Ruf.Oss.18: Comp., Arist.Phgn.809b21

ὑποκολλάω.definition: glue underneath, HeroSpir.1.32, Aut.26.5, PAmh.2.137.13 , PLips.36.10 , PMag.Lond.46.208

ὑποκόπτω.definition: cut under or beneath, Str.16.4.10; hamstring, Plu.Eum.7; D.H.6.33; J.BJ6.8.4: metaph., ib.5.1.4; ib.6.1.3

ὑποκόρισις.definition: use of the diminutive form, Eust.1196.14; euphemism, Gal.18.236

ὑποκόρισμα.definition: a coaxing or endearing name, as; a fair name for something base, as for Alex.178.2, cf. 219.5; for Plu.2.807e; so Id.Galb.20

ὑποκουρίζομαι.definition: dialect-form of coax or soothe with soft names, of the serenades sung by girls on the evening of a friend's marriage, Pi.P.3.19; cf. Hsch. s.v. cites Act. with the expl

ὑποκουφίζω.definition: intr., to be lighter, easier, of fevers, Hp.Epid.1.7: so in Pass., Orib.Syn.9.26.3

ὑποκρεμάννυμι.definition: underpin, shore up; Pass., to be hung underneath, dub. l. in Plu.2.624b

ὑποκυβερνάω.definition: to be under-pilot, of a ship, Poll.1.98

ὑποκυρτόομαι.definition: Pass., to be or become somewhat curved, Callisth. ap. Eust.918.40:—Act. in Gloss

ὑποκωθωνίζομαι.definition: indulge in deep potations, Anon. ap. An.Ox.2.414

ὑποκωμῳδέω.definition: play up to a lead, Luc.Tox.14

ὑπολαμβάνω.definition: also , late Dor. 3pl. fut. Anon.Oxy.410.99:-take up by getting under, as the dolphin did Arion, Hdt.1.24, Pl.R.453d; Arist.HA619b34; Clearch.73; Act.Ap.1.9. b. bear up, support, Hdt.4.72; Str.14.2.5, cf. D.S.19.67; BG…

ὑπολάμπω.definition: begin to shine, Hdt.1.190, cf. Ael.NA8.22; ib.10.50; Plu.Ant.49: metaph., Poll.2.87

ὑπολαπάσσω.definition: empty from below, purge, Ael.NA14.14, Phot

ὑπολευκανθίζω.definition: become whitish on the surface, Ruf. ap. Orib.8.24.64, Philum.Ven.35.2

ὑπολευκόχρως.definition: of whitish skin or complexion, Hp.Epid.1.19

ὑπολιγαίνω.definition: make to sound a little, Ach.Tat.1.5

ὑπολιμπάνω.definition: collat. form of leave behind, 1; Med., leave over, leave no arrears , PHib.1.45.13 ; reserve, PSI4.392.4

ὑπολισθάνω.definition: and slip or slide slightly, Hp.Art.5, Poll.2.15: metaph., Ael.VH2.35; Luc.Dem.Enc.12

ὑπολογέω.definition: take account of, Arist.Pol.1325a39; deduct, esp. from a sum due, IG12.207.73 , cf. PCair.Zen. 257.12, 317.11, al. , PRev.Laws 28.16 , PTeb.61.391, 72.396 : Poll.2.122 cites from Theopomp.Com.96

ὑπολογισμός.definition: consideration, reason, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.173 ; became gradually demoralized, D.H.15.3

ὑπόλογος.definition: held accountable or liable; reckoned to one's account, either to one's credit or against one, . . Pl.Prt.349c, cf. D.36.48; Lys.28.13; Pl.La.189b

ὑπόλοιπος.definition: left over, with the; of things, = still remains for you, Ar.Pl.431; And.1.109; the residue, Pl.R.427e, POxy.1252v.36 , etc.; all that remained to be done, Th.4.90; what remained to effect their destruction, Id.8.26; i…

ὑπολυπέομαι.definition: to be grieved at heart, LXX2 Ma.4.37

ὑπολυσσάω.definition: Ion. have a kind of madness, Hp.Hebd.51

ὑπομαίνομαι.definition: Pass., to be somewhat mad, Hp.Vict.1.35, Men.Epit.457

ὑπομαλακίζομαι.definition: Pass., grow cowardly by degrees, X.An.2.1.14

ὑπομαλάσσω.definition: Att. soften by degrees or gently, Aristaenet.1.3; relax, Dsc.5.7:—Pass., to be gradually softened, Luc.DMeretr.4.2

ὑπομαντεύομαι.definition: divine partly, Pl.Sis.388b; hint prophetically, . . Eust.777.49

ὑπομαραίνομαι.definition: Pass., wither or waste gradually, Ph.2.252, Plu.2.411e, Ptol.Tetr.101

ὑπομάσσω.definition: Att. smear or rub underneath, Theoc.2.59; lying close under, Anon. ap. Suid

ὑπομεθύω.definition: to be somewhat drunk, Hsch. s.v

ὑπομειδιάω.definition: smile a little or gently, Anacreont.27A.14, Phld.Vit.p.31 J., Plu.Dio20, Hld.7.10, Alciphr.3.3, etc.; Plb.18.7.6

ὑπομειόομαι.definition: Pass., to be diminished a little or gradually, Gal.19.375

ὑπομέμφομαι.definition: blame a little or secretly, Plu.Cat.Mi.15, Nonn.D.15.289, etc

ὑπομηλαφάω.definition: probe to the bottom, probe thoroughly, Hsch., Phot.,EM783.12

ὑπομηλίζω.definition: to be or look yellowish, Dsc.3.68

ὑπομιλτόομαι.definition: Pass., to be covered with ruddle, Sch.Od.5.245

ὑπομιμέομαι.definition: imitate a little, f.l. in D.S.13.95

ὑπομνηματίζομαι.definition: Med., note down for remembrance; write memoirs or annals, Plb.5.33.5; Str.2.1.9:—Pass., to be recorded, LXX1 Es.6.22; so freq. in Pap., PHamb.29.15 , cf. PRyl. 77.46 , etc

ὑπομνημάτιον.definition: Dim. of Parth.Epist.Dedic.2, PMich.Teb.123rii 19, al. , M.Ant.3.14

ὑπομνηματισμός.definition: memorandum, of a shoppinglist; note-taking, Ath.Med. ap. Orib.inc.21.6

ὑπομνηματογραφέω.definition: discharge function of; Med., write down as a memorandum, TheanoEp.6.4

ὑπομνηματογράφος.definition: in pl., memoir-writers; recorder, name of a great official in the Egyptian king's household, and the corresponding official in the office of the minister of finance , and prob. in those of other high officials, PMich.…

ὑπομνηστεύομαι.definition: Med., betroth one's daughter, Arist.Pol.1304a14:—Pass., one betrothed, ib.a 15

ὑπομόχλιον.definition: the fulcrum of a lever, Arist.Mech.850a35, al., Ph.Bel.59.21

ὑπονεφελίζω.definition: to be clouded or turbid, ib.625

ὑπονοέω.definition: surmise, conjecture, guess at, Ar.Eq.652, Lys.1234; And.1.139: c. acc. et inf., Cratin.Jun.10: abs., Ar.Lys.38; by conjecture, Pl.Grg.454c; . . , Men.261; leaving us to guess at . . , Alex.267.6

ὑπονοθεύω.definition: procure by corruption, LXX2 Ma.4.7, cf. Cat.Cod.Astr.1.98

ὑπονομεύω.definition: undermine, sap, Din. ap. Phot., Anon. ap; metaph., stir up by secret arts, stratagems, or intrigues, D.H.3.23:—Pass., v.l. for LXX2 Ma.4.26

ὑπονομή.definition: underground passage, mine, Str.13.1.67; metaph., in pl., secret stratagems or intrigues, Hsch

ὑπόνομος.definition: underground, sewers, App.BC4.13; J.AJ7.9.6; Str.13.1.67; of a lake, Id.12.8.19

ὑπονοσέω.definition: to be somewhat affected , of the spleen. Hp.Morb.4.57; sicken, of a person, Id.Epid.1.3, Luc.Tox.29, Merc. Cond.42

ὑπονοστέω.definition: go down, sink, Arist.Mete.367a24; settle, turn into a thing, Plu.2.811e: metaph., sink, decline, Longin.3.1; Dam.Pr.440; of the aged, decline in years, Poll.2.21

ὑπονοτίζω.definition: moisten underneath or a little, Hp.Epid.7.83, Placit.2.20.15

ὑπονύσσω.definition: prick or sting underneath: generally, sting, Theoc.19.3; prick, Ael.NA2.50; prod, goad, Hld.10.28; LXXIs.58.3:—Pass., Hsch

ὑπονυστάζω.definition: nod a little, fall asleep gradually, Pl.Smp.223d, Plu.2.178f

ὑποξηραίνω.definition: trans., dry up a little, in Pass., Hp.Morb.1.15, 3.16, Thphr.HP4.2.4, Gal.6.434

ὑποξυράω.definition: or shave or cut off some of the hair, Hippiatr.77:—Pass., Archil.58; Luc.DMort.9.4, Tim.22

ὑπόξυρος.definition: cut away as if by a razor, of an aquiline nose, Hp.Epid.6.8.26; i. e. flattened, Id.Prorrh.2.23, as Littré after Gal.19.149, cf. Art.77

ὑποπαίζω.definition: play or joke a little, Ael.NA12.21; trans., poke fun at, Sch.Ar.Ach.331

ὑποπαραιτέομαι.definition: beg off, Sammelb.4630.4 ; to be an excuse, Ph.2.379; disclaim, Phld.Herc. 1457.8

ὑποπαραιτία.definition: denial, refusal to recognize, dub.l. in Sammelb.3924.42

ὑποπάσχω.definition: suffer slightly or secretly, in part. Hsch

ὑποπαύομαι.definition: Pass., cease gradually, of the Nile, Ath.7.301c

ὑποπέρδομαι.definition: Med., break wind a little, Ar.Ra.1097

ὑποπερικλάομαι.definition: Pass., to be broken or bent round a little, Dsc.3.68

ὑποπετάννυμι.definition: spread out under, lay under, Od.1.130; Hp.Fist.7:—Pass., Luc.Fug.25

ὑποπηδάω.definition: leap forth or up, J.BJ4.1.9, Ael.NA12.15

ὑποπιθηκίζω.definition: play the ape a little, Ar.V.1290; cf

ὑποπίμπλημι.definition: fill, Ael.NA1.23; Pass., of women, become mothers of many children, Hdt.6.138: abs., become pregnant, Ael.NA12.21, Poll.3.49

ὑποπίμπρημι.definition: aor. 1 (the only tense in; burn as on a funeral-pyre, Hdt.2.111, 3.45

ὑποπίνω.definition: drink a little, drink moderately; drink at dessert, Ar.Av.494 , Pherecr.153.5 , X.Cyr.8.4.9, etc

ὑποποδίζω.definition: = Sch. Ar.Av.382; of planets, retrace their path, Paul.Al.C.1, al., Procl.Hyp.1.14, al

ὑποπόδιον.definition: footstool, IG22.1394.15 , Chares2 J., Schwyzer200 , PTeb.45.38 , LXXPs.98.5, Luc.Hist.Conscr.27, Sor.1.68, 29

ὑποπολιτεύομαι.definition: make one's measures subservient to, Poll.4.36

ὑποποτίζω.definition: give to drink a little, Hsch. s.v

ὑποπροχέω.definition: pour forth under, cj. in AP9.314.4

ὑποπτάζομαι.definition: to be suspected, being suspected through . . , Paul. Aeg.3.5

ὑποπτεύω.definition: merely, suspect, guess, suppose, opp. Pl.Tht.164a, cf. X.HG5.4.29; have an inkling of, Pl.Grg.453b; X.Eq.6.14:—Pass., to be conjectured, Pl.Lg.967b

ὑπόπτης.definition: suspicious; of a horse, shy, X.Eq.3.9, Sch.Th.l.c

ὑστερίζω.definition: fut. Att. D.4.32, Arist.Ph.262b17: aor; metaph., lag behind, be or become inferior to, c. gen., . . Id.Mem.3.5.13; opp. Arist.Rh.Al.1420a18

ὑστερογενής.definition: not appearing until after the birth; generally, later in origin, opp. Id.Metaph.1091a33, cf. Nicom.Ar.1.4, S.E.M.7.225, Iamb.Comm. Math.10, Herm.in Phdr.p.154A.; later in date, Str.11.5.5

ὑστερόποινος.definition: avenging after the act, late- avenging, A.Ag.58, Ch.383

ὑστερόποτμος.definition: supposed dead, and then appearing alive, Plu.2.265a, Hsch

ὑστερόπους.definition: neut. gen. coming late, Ar.Lys.326 ; AP12.229 ; Orph.A.1164

ὑστεροφθόρος.definition: destroying after the act, late- destroying, S.Ant.1074

ὐύζω.definition: make the sound of owls, v.l. for in Poll.5.90

ὑφαίρεσις.definition: taking away from under; purloining, pilfering, from the clerks' office, Test. ap. D.45.61; PSI10.1128.23 , cf. MitteisChr.372 ii 8, iii 5

ὑφαλμυρίζω.definition: to be or taste somewhat salt, Id.1.14, Plu.2.669b

ὑφάλμυρος.definition: somewhat salt, Dsc.2.122; f.l. for , Id.3.136

ὑφάντης.definition: weaver, Pl.Phd.87b, R.369d, Arist.Pol.1291a13, LXXEx.26.1, PCair.Zen.80.10 , etc

ὑφαντοδόνητος.definition: poet. swung in the weaving, woven, Ar.Av.943

ὑφαντοποιέομαι.definition: Med., weave a web, gloss on Sch.D.9.17

ὕφαντρον.definition: wage for weaving, PSI6.599.8 : pl., PEnteux.4.4 , PTeb.117.47, al. , PLond.3.1168 intr. p.136

ὑφάπτω.definition: Ion. set on fire from underneath; metaph., inflame unperceived, X.Cyr.5.1.16

ὑφαρμόζω.definition: Att. fit under , Hp.Art.7: —Pass., Ptol.Alm.5.1; Philostr.Im.2.15

ὑφαρπάζω.definition: Ion. Hdt. :—snatch away; take away underhand, filch, Ar.Eq.56; Id.Th.205, Ec.722:—Med., ib.921 ; snap up the meaning of a sentence, Id.Nu.490

ὕφασμα.definition: woven robe, web, Od.3.274, A.Ag.1492 , Ch.27 , 231,1015, E.Hel.1243, Ion1417, Pl.Plt.310e, Archestr.Fr.15.6, POxy.1428.10 , etc.; Aret.CA2.6 , cf

ὑφεδρία.definition: a sitting under, lower seat, opp. Suid

ὑφεξαιρέω.definition: = make an exception of, PLond.1.113 iv 22 ; eliminate, Zos.Alch.p.157 B

ὑφηγέομαι.definition: pf. :—go just before; c. acc. cogn., show the way, Plu.Pomp.76, etc.; gave these instructions, Lys.33.3:—Pass., the precepts laid down by us, Ael.Tact.Prooem.6:—but

ὑφήγησις.definition: leading, guidance, Hp.Nat.Puer.18; direction, Onos.Praef.3 , Iamb.VP21.96:—in Paus.7.24.8 is prob. cj

ὑφηγητής.definition: guide, leader, S.OC502; teacher, master, Plu.Dem.5, Ph.1.36, al

ὑφιζάνω.definition: = Arist.HA637b8; Pyrgio; sink, settle down, App.Mith.36, cf. Arr.An.2.27.4, Gal.10.973, Procop.Goth.4.11

ὑφιστάω.definition: late form of Sch.Il.18.600; also Dam.Pr.270

ὑφόρασις.definition: = suspicion, Plb.30.4.3, Phld.Ir.p.49 W., Plu.2.479b, D.L.2.99: c. gen., J.AJ17.12.2

ὑφοράω.definition: aor. , look at from below, eye stealthily, view with suspicion or jealousy, suspect, X.An.2.4.10; . . S.Ichn.172 :—Pass., D.11.4, Plu.Rom.8:— freq. in Med., , in same sense, Th.3.40, X.Mem.2.7.12, Is.2.7, D.18.43, Ari…

ὑφορθόω.definition: late form of re-erect, prob. in PHamb.23.27

ὑφορμίζομαι.definition: Pass. and Med., come to anchor, Th.2.83 codd. ; Plu.Sol.9: metaph., to be found under or in a place, Philostr.Her.1.3

ὑψαυχενέω.definition: carry the neck high, show off, D.H.7.46, Ph.1.145, al., LXX2 Ma.15.6, Plu.2.324e, Poll.2.135; of the cock, Ael.NA4.29

ὑψηλολογέομαι.definition: speak proudly, Pl.R.545e, Them.Or.23.291a:— Act., ib.31.354c

ὑψηλοταπείνωμα.definition: ups and downs of fortune, vicissitudes, Paul.Al.M.3: cf

ὑψηλόφωνος.definition: with high or loud voice, Sch.rec.S.El.243

ὑψιβόας.definition: loud-shouter, name of a frog in Batr.202

ὑψιβρεμέτης.definition: high-thundering, epith. of Zeus, Il.1.354, 12.68, Od.5.4, Hes.Op.8, etc.; in mock heroic lines, Ar.Lys.773, cf. Luc.Tim.4

ὑψιγέννητος.definition: born on high, its topmost shoot, A.Eu.43

ὑψικρατέω.definition: rule aloft or on high, Phot., Suid

ὑψίκρημνος.definition: with high crags, Hom.Epigr.6.5; built on a high crag, A.Pr.421 , cf. Fr.32

ὑψίλοφος.definition: high-crested, Pi.O.13.111; AP5.152 ; v.l. in Ar.Ra.818 for in Hp.Ep.16 the best codd. have

ὑψιπέτηλος.definition: Ion. and Ep. for used like of trees, Il.13.437, Od.4.458, 11.588

ὑψίπυλος.definition: with high gates, Il.6.416, 16.698, E.HF1030 , B.8.46

ὑψίπυργος.definition: high-towered, Simon.112, A.Eu.688, S.Tr.354, E.Tr.376, etc.: metaph., towering hopes, A.Supp.97

ὑψιτέλεστος.definition: prob. f. l. for late- finished, Nonn.D.41.94

ὑψιφαής.definition: high-shining, far-seen, AP7.701 ; PMag. Leid.V.8.2:—also IG22.3639.1: metaph., eminent, B.13.5:—also Ph.Epic. ap. Eus.PE9.37

ὑψιφοίτης.definition: one who wanders or moves on high, Hsch., Phot.; = Id

ὑψόροφος.definition: high-roofed, high-ceiled, Il.3.423, 24.192, Od.2.337, al.; 10.474, al.: cf

ὑψόω.definition: lift high, raise up, Batr.81, APl.4.41; metaph., elevate, exalt, opp. LXXEx.15.2, al., Plb.5.26.12, Ev.Matt.23.12, al.; [Men.] ap. Clem.Al.Strom.5.14.120:—Pass., to be exalted, LXXDe.8.14; Plu.2.103e; AP5.91 ; of sudd…

ὑπένερθε.definition: also Adv. underneath; under the earth, in the nether world, Il.3.278, 20.61, Archil.17; opp. Pl.Ax.371b, cf. A.R.2.259

ὑπεραγόντως.definition: Adv. exceedingly, LXX2 Ma.7.20, OGI315.51 , Hsch. s.v

ὑπεράνωθεν.definition: Adv. from above, LXXPs.77.23; c. gen., above, LXXEz.1.25, Aesop.4

ὑπερβεβλημένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of beyond all measure, immoderately, Arist.EN1118a7

ὑπέρευ.definition: Adv., exceedingly well, excellently, Pl.Tht.185d, X.Hier.6.9, D.18.10, Men.Pk.404, Zeno Stoic.1.27, Cic.Att.10.1.3:— Men.Epit.308, Luc.Par.9, Ael.VH9.38

ὑπεροργώντως.definition: Adv., with eager desire, Hsch. s.v

ὑπέρφευ.definition: Adv. = excessively, overmuch, A.Ag.377 ; Id.Pers.820; E.Ph.550; Id.HF1321:—Hsch. explains it by and in Phryn.PSp.89B. we have

ὑποβεβηκότως.definition: Adv. downwards, by a non-recurring; in a subordinate way, opp. Nicom.Ar.2.20.2

ὑποβλεπτικῶς.definition: Adv. with look askance, gloss on Eust.59.2; so gloss on Sch.Nic.Th.457

ὑποβλήδην.definition: Dor. Dius ap.Stob.4.21.17:—Adv; speaking in turn, Coluth.146

ὑπόβρυχα.definition: Adv. under water, Od.5.319; . . Hdt.7.130; Arat.425, cf. Opp.H.1.145, Q.S.13.485, 14.619, etc

ὑπονομηδόν.definition: Adv. underground, by means of pipes, Th.6.100

ὑποπεπτωκότως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Act. of submissively, Plb.35.2.13

ὑπόπροσθεν.definition: Adv. just before, Hp.Epid.3.2, cf. Theol.Ar.13, 16

ὑράξ.definition: Adv. promiscuously, Hsch.; Aeol. Theognost.Can.23, interpol. in Suid

ὑφειμένως.definition: Adv. pf. part. Pass. of in a subdued tone or manner, X.An.7.7.16, Philostr.VS1.25.5; Aristid.2.137J

ὑφέν.definition: earlier Adv. in one, as a single word; the hyphen, a sign written below two consecutive letters to show that they belong to the same word, D.T.Supp.674.4, Sch.D.T.p.126H., Diom.p.434 K., PAmh. 2.21.6

ὑψόσε.definition: Adv. of motion, aloft, on high, Il.10.465, Od.9.240; Il.10.461; 18.211; 21.302, cf. 324; 11.307, cf. Od.12.238; high reaching, 19.38. The two editions by Aristarchus gave and respectively in Il.10.465, 505, cf. Od.12.249
